label: Topological Spaces
notes: Open the chapter, the heart of point-set topology. The chapter spans printed pages 73 through 144 and defines topological spaces and the open sets that constitute a topology, the basis that generates them, key constructions like the subspace and product topologies, and the central notion of a continuous function between spaces.

label: Topologies and Bases
notes: Define a topology on a set as a collection of open sets closed under arbitrary unions and finite intersections, containing the whole space and the empty set. A basis generates a topology by taking unions. The standard, order, and lower-limit topologies on the real line illustrate how different bases yield genuinely different spaces.

label: Closed Sets and Closure
notes: Closed sets are complements of open sets. The closure of a set is the smallest closed set containing it, and the interior the largest open set inside it. A point lies in the closure exactly when every neighborhood meets the set, giving the limit-point description that connects topology to convergence.

label: Subspace and Product Topologies
notes: Two fundamental constructions: the subspace topology, where open sets are intersections with a subset, and the product topology, generated by products of open sets. The product topology on infinite products uses only finitely many constraints, a subtle choice that makes Tychonoff's theorem and continuity of projections work correctly.

label: Continuous Functions
notes: A function is continuous when the preimage of every open set is open, generalizing the epsilon-delta definition. Homeomorphisms are continuous bijections with continuous inverse, the isomorphisms of topology. Pasting continuous pieces and forming continuous maps into products give the practical tools for building and recognizing continuous functions.

label: Metric Topology
notes: Metric spaces supply the motivating examples: open balls form a basis, and continuity recovers the familiar analytic definition. Not every topology comes from a metric, raising the metrization question pursued later. We close with the convergence of sequences and why metric spaces behave so well.
